production.note: US model years: KBB lists the 812 Superfast for 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2021 (its 2022 address leads back to the 2021 car). In calendar years: Ferrari announced the car on 16 February 2017 for the Geneva show (ferrari-corp-812-release); The Car Expert says 'it was launched in 2017 as a replacement for the Ferrari F12 Berlinetta, and remained in production until 2023' (carexpert-812); PistonHeads says Ferrari 'stopped taking orders for the 812 Superfast coupe and GTS convertible in early 2022, although production continued until all outstanding orders had been fulfilled' (pistonheads-812-guide); Evo's title says '(2017 - 2024)', which appears to cover the whole 812 family (evo-812). The 812 GTS and 812 Competizione are separate models.

body.note: Ferrari: 'the new 12-cylinder berlinetta, the 812 Superfast'. The open 812 GTS is a separate model.

fuel.note: Not stated in so many words; petrol V12 with a fuel consumption figure in l/100km and no hybrid system.

drivetrain.note: Spec panel: 'Transmission | Seven-speed dual-clutch, rear-wheel drive'

transmission.note: Evo spec panel: 'Seven-speed dual-clutch, rear-wheel drive'. Ferrari's release says 'The 812 Superfast's dual-clutch transmission has specific gear ratios' without giving the number of gears (ferrari-corp-812-release). Ferrari calls it the F1 DCT. No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Ferrari's rating is metric: 800 cv x 0.98632 = 789 hp. Quote (Ferrari press release): "Maximum power output * | 588 kW (800 cv) at 8,500 rpm", footnote "*With 5 cv ram effect". No separate SAE rating for the US was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS; publications print the same 789 (Evo spec panel: '789bhp @ 8500rpm'; PistonHeads: 'Power (hp) | 789@8,500rpm'; KBB's US listing: '789 hp').

weightLb.note: 1,630 kg x 2.20462 = 3,594 lb. Coupe with the 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox (the only configuration). Quote (Evo spec panel): "Weight | 1630kg (492bhp/ton)". PistonHeads' spec panel gives the same: "Weight (kg) | 1,630" (pistonheads-812-guide), and KBB's US listing shows a curb weight of '3593 lbs.' (kbb-812, the same figure truncated). Neither magazine panel labels the figure kerb or dry. Ferrari's press release gives only a dry weight: "Dry weight** | 1,525 kg", footnote "**With lightweight optionals" (ferrari-corp-812-release). 1,630 kg is exactly 105 kg above that optioned dry weight, so it very probably also assumes the lightweight options. No US-specific figure was found. Under the guide's weight order this is step 3 (a curb weight for a car with lightweight options; here very probably Ferrari's unnamed lightweight options), adopted on 2 October 2026: no curb weight for a standard car was found, and a standard car is somewhat heavier.

discrepancies.reason: Dry vs kerb. Ferrari's launch release gives only a dry weight, and that figure is 'With lightweight optionals'. Evo's and PistonHeads' specification panels both print 1,630 kg.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the published kerb figure under weight step 3 (an optioned car's curb weight), since no standard-car curb weight was found and a curb weight ranks above a dry weight.

reviewNotes: Last US model year: 2021 rests on KBB's model-year list alone; UK sources say orders closed in early 2022 and production ran on into 2023, so a 2022 US model year cannot be ruled out.
